Directions: Read the passage below, then answer each question that follows.
Title: [from] What Are the Parts of Government?
Author: by William David Thomas
Content: Kylie really liked basketball. Her older sister, Kelcey, was a star on the high school team. Kelcey was also a star in the classroom, and she was helping Kylie get ready for a social studies test.
“I just don’t get it!” said Kylie.
“Well look,” said Kelcey, “the government is a lot like basketball.”
“You have got to be kidding!”

“I’m serious,” said Kelcey. “The U.S. Constitution is the highest law in the land. It sets up `text(three)` parts, or branches, of government. They’re the executive branch, the legislative branch, and the judicial branch. `text(Each one)` has a different job to do.” . . .
The President

The president heads up the executive branch of government. The U.S. Constitution says the president must “take care that the laws be faithfully `ultext(executed)`.” To enforce the laws, the president has certain powers.

:ibox:• As chief executive, the president oversees the major offices of the U.S. government. The president chooses the people who lead those offices.
• The president is commander-in-chief of the armed forces, which includes the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marines.
• The president can make `ultext(treaties)` with foreign countries.
• The president may veto, or reject, a bill passed by Congress.
• As head of state, the president is a symbol of the nation. The president represents the country at home and abroad.

The president has great powers. But those powers are controlled by the Constitution. The system is called “checks and balances.” It keeps any part of the government from becoming too powerful. For example, the president commands the armed forces. However, only Congress can declare war. The president can make treaties with foreign countries. But the treaties must be approved by Congress before they can go into effect.
The Vice President
The vice president is the `text(second)` highest-ranking person in the government. The vice president becomes president if:

:ibox:• the president dies in office (this has happened `text(eight)` times)
• the president resigns (this has only happened `text(once)`)
• the president is removed from office by Congress (this has never happened)

The Constitution gives the vice president `text(one)` responsibility — president of the Senate. If a vote in the Senate ends in a tie, the vice president votes to break the tie. The vice president also works with leaders in Congress and helps the president make decisions.

Long ago, there was no vice presidential candidate on the ballot. People only voted for the president. The person with the most votes became president. The person in `text(second)` place became the vice president. This was changed by the `text(Twelfth)` Amendment to the Constitution. Since `1804`, people have voted for the president and vice president as a team. . . .
Federal Agencies
Many federal agencies are part of the executive branch, too. These agencies advise the president on such things as national security, . . . trade, the budget, and science. Some of these agencies are:

:ibox:• the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA)
• the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)
• the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
Altogether, nearly `text(three million)` people work in the executive branch. With the president, they “take care that the laws be faithfully executed.” . . .
The Powers of Congress
Congress is the legislative branch of the government. That means it is the law-making branch. Congress meets in the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.
Congress does much more than make laws. The Constitution gives this branch of government many powers. . . .
`text(One)` Congress, `text(Two)` Houses

Congress has `text(two)` parts, or houses. The House of Representatives has `435` members. `text(Each state)` has a different number of representatives. The number depends on the state’s population. California has `text(fifty-three)` representatives. Vermont has only `text(one)`. Members of the House serve a term that lasts `text(two years)`. They can be re-elected many times.

The other house of Congress is the Senate. There are `text(one hundred)` senators. `text(Each state)` has `text(two)` senators, no matter what the population. `text(Each senator)` serves a term of `text(six years)`. They too may be re-elected. . . .
The Supreme Court

The Supreme Court is the highest court in the United States. Its most important job is to `ultext(interpret)` the U.S. Constitution. The Constitution was written more than `text(two hundred years)` ago. The Court must decide how the rules in the Constitution apply to what happens today.

The Court can decide that a law is unconstitutional. If that happens, the law is nullified. That means it is no longer a law. The Court can also decide that actions taken by Congress or the president are unconstitutional. If so, those actions must stop.

There are no juries in the Supreme Court. There are `text(nine)` judges, called justices. `text(One)` of them is the chief justice. When the Court hears a case, all `text(nine)` justices listen. They discuss the case. Then they vote. A simple majority — just `text(five)` votes — is all that is needed to decide a case. . . .

The Supreme Court has made decisions about slavery, religion, and even presidential elections. The Court’s rulings are often controversial. The justices have to stay calm and think clearly. Oliver Wendell Holmes was a famous justice. He `text(once)` said, “We are very quiet here, but it is the quiet of a storm center.”

:box:`bbtext(Glossary)`

`ultext(executed)`: put into effect

`ultext(treaties)`: agreements

`ultext(interpret)`: explain

`ultext(juries)`: people who make decisions in a case
